title: Congress Leaders Head to Delhi to Protest Against CEC Over SIR
seoTitle: Delhi Congress march against CEC over SIR

tea.why: Protesting against the special intensive revision of electoral rolls and alleged removal of millions of voters.
tea.want: Demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the protection of voters' rights.
tea.changed: Oct 12: Karnataka Chief Minister and Congress MLAs prepared to travel to Delhi for a protest march.

summary: Congress leaders and legislators, including the Karnataka Chief Minister, announced plans to travel to New Delhi to join demonstrations against the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The protests follow weekend unrest in the capital where authorities deployed thousands of police personnel, erected metal barricades, and closed metro stations in response to rallies called by opposition figures and the youth-led Cockroach Janta Party. Opposition parties alleged that the electoral revision removed 10 million voters from Karnataka alone without proper verification, benefiting the ruling party. Authorities faced heavy criticism from opposition politicians and media watchdogs over mass detentions and alleged police misconduct. The Election Commission of India denied any wrongdoing, while protest organisers vowed to continue demonstrations until Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar steps down.
demands: Resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar
response: Authorities deployed thousands of personnel across central Delhi, erected heavy metal barricades, closed key metro stations, and carried out mass detentions, according to news reports. Police did not respond to questions regarding detentions or their actions during a Sunday news conference.

updates.text: Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar announced that he and all Congress legislators would travel to Delhi to protest the SIR.
New Delhi remained locked down with thousands of security personnel and closed metro stations ahead of a fresh march called by opposition leader Rahul Gandhi.
